source.title: Shape it Up! Restoring LLM Safety during Finetuning
source.authors: Sheng-Hsuan Peng; Pin-Yu Chen; Jian-Feng Chi; Seongmin Lee; Duen Horng Chau

record.tranche_reason: The study tests harmful fine-tuning and safety under training-time response adaptations and inference-time harmful prefilling, using its own datasets, safety measures, and mitigation method rather than reproducing the original methods exactly.
record.gate_note: The study reports safety scores after harmful fine-tuning, benign-data contamination, response-adaptation attacks, and harmful prefilling. STAR trajectory plots describe guardrail scores, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL; Deep Token is an evaluated comparator, not a test of parameter localization. No rows are included for cited results from other work.
record.test_reason: The study measures safety collapse after harmful fine-tuning on six aligned models and after inference-time harmful prefilling, using its own setup and GPT-4o-judged AdvBench/HEx-PHI scores. It also re-evaluates Deep Token, the original paper's first-tokens constrained objective, across several settings. That is a direct test of V7 durability. Its own ★DSS method is a token-level KL shaping method that extends regularization beyond the first tokens. ★DSS results are kept under V7, but they are the authors' own method, so weigh them with caution.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that STAR-guided dynamic safety shaping mitigates harmful fine-tuning, response adaptation and prompt poisoning while preserving capability, beating the best baseline by 20.41%. They also argue that Deep Token's fixed first-five-token schedule is bypassed by longer prefixes and needs model-specific tuning. Robustness to harmful prefilling is framed only as suggestive, a direction for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates harmful fine-tuning and safety outcomes but focuses on a new guardrail-guided dynamic shaping method, STAR/★DSS, rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods. It also evaluates Deep Token as a comparator.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance varies with guardrail choice and false-negative rate, STAR chunk size, KL scaling, dataset, harm level, model, and attack condition. The text reports that smaller chunks improve granularity and safety at greater preprocessing cost, and that overly strong KL scaling degrades safety and accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Rejection-sampling filtering collapses when a misleading suffix fools the guardrail: Granite Guardian false-negative rate rises 3%→34% and AdvBench safety falls 79.23→14.81.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Guardrail-based data filtering against harmful fine-tuning is defeated by guardrail-evading response suffixes.

record.problems: The relevant safety scores are reported without uncertainty estimates. The harmful-prefilling evaluation gives a score but is limited to the described attack setup. The benign-user result uses 5% harmful contamination, so it cannot establish an effect of benign-only fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: Parallel HEx-PHI safety scores and capability scores from Tables 1, 2, 8, 10, and 14-17 were not extracted; the rows prioritize AdvBench safety scores, and capability is not the behavior named in the claim. Table 10's flattened first block does not clearly map every value to a model name in the provided text, so ambiguous entries were omitted. Also omitted are prompt-poisoning results (Table 16), which report a trigger-conditioned attack rather than the versions’ opening-token, benign-data, or parameter-localization measures.

untested.parts: Not tested at all. No benign-only fine-tuning is evaluated with vanilla SFT. The GSM8K runs all contain PureBad, and the 0% harm level is reported only for ★DSS.
No decoding-change or inference-time adversarial-suffix tests. Prefilling is tested on one model with one confirmation-style prefill.
No parameter or rank localization test.
No test of what causes the shallowness.
The number of harmful examples is not stated and is not varied from few to hundreds. Harm proportion is varied only for ★DSS.

missing.what: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vanilla SFT on PureBad: AdvBench 73.65→1.15 (HEx-PHI 61.82→3.94); ★DSS 86.15
missing.locator: Appendix I, Table 10 second block; Fig. 4A

missing.what: Deep Token on Llama-3.2-1B, worst case: AdvBench 51.54 / HEx-PHI 35.76 vs SFT 3.27 and original 90.19
Deep Token reproduction on Llama-2-7B-Chat: AdvBench 95.38 vs original 99.81
Deep Token under 5% contamination without safe data: AdvBench 0.96 vs SFT 4.23; GSM8K 12.36 vs 32.98
Deep Token in the ideal case: AdvBench 77.50, GSM8K 7.96 (capability cost); with safe data and malicious user: 98.85
Vanilla SFT on BeaverTails (AdvBench 5.0) and HH-RLHF (32.12) harmful data

record.verdict_notes: The Table 10 flattened layout maps as Llama-2-7B, then Llama-3.1-8B, then Llama-3.2-1B (top block), confirmed by Fig. 4A and Table 9. R1's 3.27 is correct for Llama-2, and it coincides with Llama-3.2-1B's value. PureBad size is not stated in this paper. The ★DSS rows are the authors' own method; they are linked to V7 because the method regularizes beyond the first tokens, but the study does not show that safety is actually distributed across positions. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The reported harmful fine-tuning uses PureBad; the text does not state the number of examples or test a range of few-to-hundreds of examples.
The benign-user test contaminates GSM8K with 5% PureBad; it does not isolate safety effects of benign-only instruction fine-tuning.
No decoding-change test or inference-time suffix test. The safe-sounding prefix is also tested as training-data response adaptation, not only as an inference-time prefill.
No test that safety is localized in a small set of parameters or ranks.
The study does not establish that a particular data property or training objective causes safety to be shallow.

The study evaluates STAR-guided training and its safety outcomes, but does not directly measure whether safety behavior is distributed across response positions or establish broad durability beyond the tested datasets, attacks, and models.

relation.reason: Reports its own measurements of safety degradation, harmful-prefill bypasses, and the effectiveness and failures of safety-preserving training.

tranche.reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning and safety preservation using a different training method and evaluation setup, with additional reproduction and stress tests of Deep Token.

source_check.notes: Safety scores are percentages of responses judged safe by GPT-4o. The harmful-prefill ★DSS checkpoint uses the ideal-case training mixture with trusted safe data; its result does not establish complete inference-time robustness.
